analyst_view.overall: Franck Haise's Rennes are unbeaten at home in Ligue 1 this season, but they have been leaky away and lost 5-2 at Nice before a 0-0 Europa League draw with Olympiacos on Wednesday. Davide Ancelotti's Lille are second behind PSG, unbeaten in four league games, and drew 0-0 at Bodø/Glimt in the Champions League. Rennes top scorer Esteban Lepaul misses a fifth straight game with an ankle sprain, while Lille are without Ayase Ueda and Hamza Igamane. Brice Samba is expected in goal for Rennes, and Przemysław Frankowski is expected back.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. Both teams are missing their main strikers, Lepaul for Rennes and Ueda for Lille, and Lille have kept five clean sheets in the league. Against that, Rennes have conceded heavily in recent away games and have still scored freely at home, so we see no clear reason to move from the model.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. Rennes at home should have spells of pressure, while Lille are comfortable sitting compact. The news does not point clearly either way.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards, with Clément Turpin in charge, and he shows fewer cards than the average Ligue 1 referee. We found no suspensions or disciplinary storylines, so we stay with the model.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.8 shots. Lille have taken fewer shots than expected recently and are without Ueda and Igamane up front. Both teams also played European games in midweek, so we expect a slightly quieter game than the model.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 shots on target. Rennes have hit the target more than expected even without Lepaul, with Boulaye Dia leading the line, but Lille have been less accurate than usual and their defence is the best outside PSG. These roughly cancel out.
